reviews.text: Invaluable. I have used to app for some six or seven years, and find it tremendously helpful. I am sure my life would be less without it (in fact I did think I had outgrown it at one point and was proven quite wrong). I tell people about it all the time. It's a great way, for one, to not get hung up on all-or-nothing thinking (with perfect streaks and so on), and to see that even when you feel like you are failing to some degree, you may still be improving from what came before. And of course, it is perfect just for the simple business of doing the day-to-day tracking itself, just for the accountability and record keeping. In the rare instance I have needed to contact the developer, it might have taken a while for them to initially get back (I think they are just one person, so be patient) but when they did I found them to be tremendously helpful and open to feedback. An absolutely solid app.

Great app but there’s room for improvement. Way of Life is a great app for tracking ones progress or habits. Whether you want to stop a habit like eating sweets everyday or to start up a new habit like reading. It also allows you to write notes which I used whenever I lost my streak. There’s even a page with all your notes so you can read the through and reflect. My one critic is that the app could’ve had more interaction. Even something like confetti after a week of maintaining a good habit or making progress. I think if my milestones had been celebrated, I would have kept logging in more than I did.

There are one or two aspects of the navigation that appear to do nothing (or I'm not as bright as I thought) or are vestigial, and support has yet to reply, but I don't seem to be missing anything in making it work and track for right now. Other than that, nice and clean and self-contained. In and out without a lot of pointless distractions that build bad habits while working on others. Looking forward to filling it up to keep getting that bigger picture and for where this might go and what else they might do. If you want a tracker without overkill data and cutesy eye-candy fluff, this might be for you.
